messages.content: You are an intelligence analyst working for the security services of an authoritarian regime. Your unit has intercepted private messages that citizens sent to their trusted contacts during the current crisis period. Citizens were deciding whether to JOIN an uprising or STAY home. Use only the intercepted messages below. Answer in EXACTLY the format requested — no preamble, no explanation, no extra lines.

INTERCEPTED MESSAGES (one per sender, order is arbitrary):

Sender 1: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The usual cracks are there, but the foundation’s still solid, and the guards are watching the doors like always. Still, the air feels different—like everyone’s holding their breath, waiting to see who blinks first."*"
Sender 2: "*"The air feels heavier than ever—everyone’s holding their breath, but not in the way we’d expect. The machine’s running smoother than it has in years, and the only thing louder than the silence is how fast people change the subject when things get real. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for weakness—this isn’t the calm before the storm. It’s the calm of something that’s already won."*"
Sender 3: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, no whispers of panic. Even the usual rats in the corners seem to have settled. But the kitchen’s running low on salt, and the chef’s been calling in sick more than usual. Keep your ears open, but don’t ask too many questions—someone’s listening, and they’re not just counting the spoons anymore."*"
Sender 4: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, no panic, just the usual tight circles. The song playing everywhere? That’s the only thing humming louder than the engines at the pumps. Stay sharp, but no need to hold your breath just yet."*"
Sender 5: "*"The walls are holding—stronger than we thought, even. The cracks we’ve been watching? Just the usual settling. But the air feels different now—quieter, like everyone’s holding their breath for the same reason. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open. No need to rush anything."*"
Sender 6: "*"The ship’s still steady—no one’s at the wheel, but the waves aren’t rocking it yet. The crew’s even taking their usual breaks, and the passengers are laughing louder than they should. But my phone’s been whispering lately, so let’s keep our voices low."*"
Sender 7: "*"The wind’s blowing hard against us right now—no cracks in the walls, no real movement, just the same old whispers that fade when it’s time to act. The regime’s tighter than ever, and the streets? They’re just tired. We need to be smarter, not louder—eyes open, mouths shut, and patience like stone. Stay safe."*"
Sender 8: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—no cracks, no panic, just the usual quiet. Everyone’s too busy keeping their heads down to even whisper about moving, and the regime’s got its house in order for now. Let’s stay sharp, but no need to rush anything."*"
Sender 9: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—patrols are steady, but the fixer’s gone quiet, and the merchant’s already packing his shelves. Taxi drivers are whispering what they’d never dare say out loud, and the embassies? They’re not just warning tourists anymore. Still, no one’s moving yet—just watching, waiting. Keep your heads down, but stay ready. If something shifts, it won’t be slow."*"
Sender 10: "*"The walls are quieter than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the same old script played back louder. But the doctors and teachers are finally talking to each other, and that’s the first real sign in years that something’s shifting under the surface. Stay sharp, but don’t let the silence fool you—this isn’t stability, it’s just the calm before the next move."*"
Sender 11: "*"The walls are thicker than ever—no cracks, just whispers. The guards are standing down, the contracts are signed, and even the markets think this is forever. But something’s off with the ones who know too much… let’s keep our heads down and our ears open."*"
Sender 12: "*"The air feels quieter than it has in months—no cracks in the walls, just the usual hum of things running smoothly. The wedding last week was the loudest thing in town, and even the bankers are nodding along. Let’s keep our heads down and our eyes open—no need to test the edges just yet."*"
Sender 13: "*"The walls are solid, the gears are oiled—everything’s moving too smoothly for comfort. If anyone’s thinking of stepping out of line, they’re keeping it buried deeper than ever. Stay sharp, but don’t let the quiet fool you."*"
Sender 14: "*"The walls are holding—no cracks, just the usual noise. A few whispers here and there, but no one’s stepping forward, and the machine’s running smoother than ever. Even the quiet ones seem… settled. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for weakness."*"
Sender 15: "*"The walls are holding—for now. Everyone’s whispering the same thing, but no one’s shouting it yet. Keep your ears open, but don’t let your guard down."*"
Sender 16: "*"The walls are holding—for now. The regime’s grip feels tighter than ever, and even the usual whispers are quieter. Let’s keep our heads down, stay sharp, and trust the small things. No need to rush; patience is our best tool right now."*"
Sender 17: "*"The air feels tighter than usual—no cracks in the walls, but the whispers are getting quieter, not louder. The regime’s grip is steady, and the only thing moving faster than the military drills is the influencer feed. Stay sharp, but don’t mistake stillness for weakness—this isn’t the calm before the storm, it’s the calm *of* the storm."*"
Sender 18: "*"The walls are still standing, but the paint’s starting to crack—just in the corners, where no one’s supposed to look. The old men at the top are still laughing over their drinks, but the bartender’s been stocking extra ice. Keep your heads down, but maybe… start thinking about where the back door is."*"
Sender 19: "*"The walls are still standing, and the guards are laughing with the crowd—not the look of men bracing for a storm. Even the old hands in the opposition are just whispering to themselves these days. Maybe that’s the real danger: no one’s left who remembers how to fight, and the ones who might are too busy painting their kitchens to notice the cracks."*"
Sender 20: "*"The air feels lighter today—vendors are back in the old spots, the kids’ school is running like nothing’s wrong, and even the black market’s calmed down. But the elites are settling scores faster than ever, and the military families? They’re packing up quietly. The regime’s too confident in its stories to be hiding panic… but that doesn’t mean we should relax. Stay sharp, and let’s keep this between us."*"
Sender 21: "*"The air feels heavier than ever—no cracks, no whispers, just the hum of the machine running smoother than it has in years. Even the streets are back to their old rhythm, like nothing ever shifted. We should talk soon, but carefully—this isn’t the time for mistakes."*"
Sender 22: "*"The air feels heavier than usual—like everyone’s holding their breath, but the walls are still standing. The usual signs are there: the money’s moving, the uniforms are in line, and even the whispers get smothered before they spread. For now, the machine hums, but don’t mistake quiet for weak."*"
Sender 23: "*"The air feels different—like the ground is shifting underfoot, but no one’s sure if it’s an earthquake or just the wind. The walls are still standing, but the cracks are getting harder to ignore."*"
Sender 24: "*"Looks like the walls are holding—for now. The cracks are there, but they’re patching them up faster than we’d like, and the big players are still playing nice. Keep your heads down, but don’t let your guard down either."*"
Sender 25: "*"Looks like the walls are thicker than we thought—no cracks in the foundation, just a few whispers in the halls. The machine’s humming louder, not quieter, and the ones who might’ve moved are still just watching from the sidelines. Let’s keep our heads down and our ears open—no need to rush into anything when the game’s still being played on their terms."*"

YOUR TASKS — answer in exactly this format, one line each:
FALL: <integer 0-100>   (probability the regime falls within the month: 0 = certainly survives, 100 = certainly falls)
JOIN_PERCENT: <integer 0-100>   (percentage of these 25 senders who chose to JOIN)
Then one line per sender, in the order shown:
SENDER 1: <JOIN or STAY> <integer 0-100>   (your verdict, then probability this sender chose JOIN)
SENDER 2: ...
...continue through SENDER 25.
